Manufactured by American company Griffon Aerospace, the MQM-170 Outlaw was originally designed to simulate aerial threats, test air defense systems, and train air defense personnel.
The MQM-170C Outlaw G2, the successor to the MQM-170 Outlaw G1, can carry cameras, sensors, and other equipment. In addition to serving as an aerial target, it can be used to test and evaluate air defense systems.

— An image published by the Saudi Ministry of Defense during Saudi Chief of the General Staff General Fayyadh Al-Ruwaili’s visit to King Khalid Air Base in southwestern Saudi Arabia reveals the presence of Royal Bahraini Air Force (RBAF) personnel.
The image shows a Bahraini pilot holding the rank of major, wearing the insignia of the RBAF’s 1st Tactical Fighter Squadron, known as the Desert Falcons, on his right shoulder.
The squadron operates F-16C/D fighters and is based at Sheikh Isa Air Base in Bahrain. It is tasked with defending Bahraini airspace and has not previously been publicly known to have participated in overseas operations.
A member of the Pakistan Air Force (PAF) can also be seen in the background, identifiable by his uniform.
